points.text: SAM-with-smoothing component follows Sharp-MAML and Random SAM; novelty is the application only.
TUH is truncated backpropagation (Shaban et al.), uncited; incremental.
Learning-rate learning in Eq. 10 already exists in MTT; incremental.
DATM omitted from main tables; SATM-DA comparison incomplete and not superior.
ImageNet-scale claim ignores decoupled/relabelling methods like RDED, not compared.
Link between data-space flatness and generalisation assumed; Fig. 2 not a sharpness measure.
Provenance of baseline numbers (copied vs reproduced) not stated.
Table 5 MTT value differs from Table 2 for same setting.
Claims of clear improvements exceed small Table 2 margins.
Four components evaluated only as a package; no ablation.
Efficiency table lacks MTT + SAM comparison.
Notation drifts between text, Algorithm 1 and Table 1; hard to re-implement.
Limitations section missing.
Numerous typos.
Assumption that data-space flatness yields transferable data is not tested.
Theory bounds loose with unrealistic assumptions; approximation errors never measured.
Experts only small ConvNets; no ResNet/ViT experts or larger settings.
Robustness of distilled data to corruptions or label noise untested.
No limitations or impact discussion.
Data-space flatness to generalisation link untested.
Generic SAM recovers most gain; smoothing contribution not ablated.
Margins mostly within one std; wording overstates.
Constant-memory and faster-than-MTT claims conflict with cost model.
Theory does not rigorously bound errors of all approximations; proofs incomplete.
Hyperparameter and baseline tuning split not stated.
ImageNet overclaim given RDED cited but not compared.
DATM absent from Tables 2-3.
Table 5 values inconsistent with Tables 2/9.
SATM-FI 'clear improvements' claim not supported.
Fig. 1 outperformance claim has no numbers.
Fig. 2 caption and text disagree on setting.
Component contributions not isolated; plain SAM recovers most gain; no ablation.
Gains mostly within noise but wording strong.
What ± covers unstated; no independent distillation runs or CIs.
Hyperparameter selection protocol and values unstated.
Constant-memory and time claims inconsistent with Table 1 and measurements.
Memory 58% above TESLA contradicts 'comparable memory' claim.
No MTT + vanilla SAM cost row to measure TUH/TR savings.
Theory does not support bounded approximation errors; no bound for Eq. 10.
Theorem 4.2 proof uses constant 2σ inconsistent with smoothness; bound nonzero at ε=0.
Proposition 4.1 proof incomplete; 2ι factor not derived.
Hyperparameter table incomplete; code only promised.
Mini-batched outer loop vs full-batch baselines; mixed GPUs.
Table 5 values conflict with Tables 2 and 9.
Figure captions conflict with text on settings.
Limited novelty: combines sharpness-aware optimization with MTT.
No comparison with other SAM-based approaches.
Missing comparisons with recent SOTA such as RDED, NRR-DD, SRe2L.
SAM introduction is a simple application.
Truncated unrolling hypergradient similar to prior k-step SGD.
Improvement over SOTA is incremental.
Latest efficient distillation SOTA methods missing.
Limited baselines: decoupled, diffusion-based, optimization-free methods missing.
Experiments limited to ConvNet architecture.
Accuracy improvements marginal, often under 1%.
No ablation of trajectory reuse and TUH.
Runtime high vs TESLA, weakening efficiency argument.
Many hyperparameters; tuning setup and transferability unclear.
Lacks discussion of related works on sharpness and dataset bias in distillation.

P.summary: ImageNet claim ignores decoupled methods like RDED.
Data-space flatness to generalisation link untested.
Theory loose; approximation errors unbounded or unmeasured.
Only ConvNet experts and small-scale settings.
Memory/time efficiency claims inconsistent with cost model.
Variance source unstated; no independent runs.
Memory higher than TESLA despite 'comparable' claim.

Q.summary: Limited novelty: SAM applied to MTT.
TUH similar to prior k-step method.
No ablation of trajectory reuse and TUH.
